evidence.claim: SQLite 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 are likely affected by the WAL-reset corruption race; fixed in 3.51.3+, with stated trigger requiring multiple connections plus concurrent write/checkpoint.
Cross-file ATTACH transactions are not crash-atomic as a set in WAL; rollback-journal mode with file-backed main is the documented atomic path.
Super-journal coordinates atomic multi-file commit under eligible rollback-journal settings.
Current upstream 3.53.3 includes the WAL-reset fix.

hypothesis_impulses.claim: A fail-closed StorageTopologyIdentity certificate can turn the current WAL/rollback choice into a testable release gate by binding sqlite_source_id, journal_mode, synchronous, VFS, database file-set, connection graph, writer/checkpointer topology, transaction scope and recovery oracle.
support: The accepted target receipts report SQLite 3.45.1, within upstream's likely affected WAL range.
Rollback DELETE/FULL gives a documented super-journal path for bounded attached pair transactions.
Current target pre-COMMIT rollback controls pass.
hypothesis_impulses.counterhypothesis: An upgraded fixed SQLite WAL build plus a mechanically single-connection or serialized writer/checkpointer topology is safer and materially faster; ClayGraph may remain asynchronous/rebuildable so pair atomicity is unnecessary outside migrations.
decisive_test: Run the real target workload under A: upgraded fixed WAL with topology instrumentation and B: DELETE/FULL attached-pair critical sections.
Inject process kill/power-loss windows during multi-file COMMIT, not only exceptions before COMMIT.
Require every recovered pair to be exactly PRE/PRE or POST/POST, never split; verify integrity, FK, schema and semantic/projection identities.
Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, lock wait, checkpoint/fsync cost and recovery time.
Fail closed if SQLite source ID/backport identity or connection/checkpoint topology is unbound.
hypothesis_impulses.promotion_rule: No storage mode promotion from upstream documentation or existing pre-COMMIT receipts alone.

support: GraphIdentityVector intentionally separates DynamicRoot from stable ProjectionIdentity.

decisive_test: Construct two admitted dynamic snapshots with identical structural/epistemic roots.
Force DynamicRoot to be causally consulted while holding final universe/ranking/selection identical.
Ask whether exact replay and causal audit contracts require distinguishable receipts; preregister the contract before observing results.

Keep result vector-valued: output integrity and causal-context integrity may pass/fail independently.
